name: X-linked Intellectual Disability-Spastic Paraplegia with Iron Deposits Syndrome
aliases: X-linked Intellectual Disability with Spastic Paraplegia and Brain Iron Accumulation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for XLID-SP Iron Deposits Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of intellectual disability ranging from moderate to severe
Progressive lower limb spasticity and weakness consistent with spastic paraplegia
Neuroimaging evidence of abnormal iron accumulation in basal ganglia or other brain regions
X-linked pattern of inheritance or affected male relatives
Identification of pathogenic variants in associated gene(s) linked to the syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of intellectual disability, spastic paraplegia, and neuroimaging evidence of brain iron deposits, plus either genetic confirmation or consistent family history.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by genetic testing and exclusion of other neurodegenerative disorders with brain iron accumulation.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically affects lower limbs with increased muscle tone and hyperreflexia

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intellectual disability of moderate to severe degree
pathognomonic.notes: Global developmental delay with cognitive impairment

pathognomonic.symptomName: Brain iron accumulation visible on MRI
pathognomonic.notes: Iron deposits primarily in basal ganglia and substantia nigra
searchTerms: iron buildup in brain seen on MRI
brain iron deposits visible on scan
excess iron accumulation in brain tissue

common.notes: Speech difficulties due to motor impairment
Exaggerated deep tendon reflexes in legs
Includes hyperactivity, irritability, or autistic features

occasional.notes: Involuntary muscle contractions causing abnormal postures
Sensory deficits or weakness in distal limbs
Including optic atrophy or decreased visual acuity

rare.notes: Spinal curvature secondary to muscle imbalance
Difficulty swallowing due to bulbar involvement

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of neurodegeneration
imaging: MRI showing hypointense signals on T2-weighted images in basal ganglia consistent with iron accumulation
Possible cerebral atrophy in advanced stages
genetic: Pathogenic variants in gene(s) linked to X-linked intellectual disability and neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation
other: Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance
Electrophysiological studies may show corticospinal tract involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset with characteristic 'eye of the tiger' sign on MRI
Lack of brain iron accumulation on imaging

redFlags: Rapid progression of spastic paraplegia with cognitive decline
Early onset of neurological symptoms in male patients
MRI evidence of brain iron accumulation in basal ganglia
references: Orphanet: X-linked intellectual disability-spastic paraplegia with iron deposits syndrome, ORPHA:85333
